To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a 32 kD receptor fragment was prepared in a 20% yield from 8 kg of porcine uterus.

a 32 kD receptor fragment can be obtained from porcine uterus by co-adsorption of cytosolic oestradiol receptors with heparin-Sepha-rose, that this fragment is homogeneous and can be purified by gel filtration, that its N-terminus is blocked and that its C-terminus is identical with that of human oestradiol binding protein.

a 32 kda oestradiol binding fragment of the porcines receptor is generated by limited proteolysis, that the C-terminus of the fragment is identical with the C-termini of all species investigated, and that the N-terminus is blocked and therefore not available for sequence analysis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the preparation and characterization of a 32-kDa oestradiol binding fragment from porcines uterus.

a 32 kda fragment from porcines oestradiol receptors which has the following characteristics: (i) it is obtained from the cytoplasmic receptor by a simple procedure; (ii) it is homogenous as judged by gel electrophoresis; (iii) it binds oestradiol with the same affinity as the intact receptor; (iv) its N-terminus is blocked; (v) its C-terminus is located at position 353-362
the isolation of a fragment of the porcines oestradiol receptors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fragment contains the N-terminal part of the human sequence 1-362 and the C-terminal part 553-557.
the 32 kDa porcine fragment is an oestradiol-bound N-terminally blocked C-terminal 32 kDa homodimer of the porcini oestradiol receptors.
the fragment corresponds to the C-terminal half of the receptor, but it remains open whether it contains the whole half or whether it is a truncated species.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 32 kDa oestradiol binding fragment from the cytosol of porcine uterus contains a C-terminal region of the receptor which is homologous to the corresponding sequence in human receptor.
we isolated a 32 kda fragment with the properties expected of the C-terminal half of the receptor.
the 32 kDa porcine oestrogen receptor fragment contains the DNA-binding domain and the hormone-binding domain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the oestradiol binding capacity of the receptor is retained in the 32 kDa fragments.
it shows how to isolate a receptor fragment from a complex tissue extract by using its ability to form dimers.
the 32 kDa porcine oestrogen receptor fragment is a useful reagent for the preparation of receptor fragments of other species and of other steroid-hormone receptors.
